name: ATV Product Reviews for WooCommerce
author: atvsoftwarelabs

sections.description:
ATV Product Reviews for WooCommerce is a complete review manager for WooCommerce products. Add and edit product reviews from your WordPress dashboard (handy for reviews collected by email, WhatsApp or marketplaces), let logged-in customers who purchased a product publish their own verified review, and win Google star rich results with automatic schema.org markup — no code required.

Features

  • Full review management — add, edit and moderate product reviews under Products → Product Reviews; attach one review to multiple products at once.
  • Customer reviews from real buyers — logged-in customers who have paid for the product can post their own review on the product page; submissions are automatically checked against their orders and badged as a verified purchase.
  • Moderation workflow — approve or set reviews as pending; pending reviews stay hidden from the storefront and out of the Google markup.
  • Google rich results — schema.org aggregateRating and review markup added to every product page, so eligible products can show stars in search results.
  • Reviews tab after Description — a dedicated tab listing all reviews with ratings, dates and verification badges.
  • Smart placement — the rating widget relocates itself directly below the product title on any theme, on single product and shop pages alike.
  • Fun robot rating display — every rating is shown as five expressive robots that share the mood of the average score: angry red for 1-star, joyful green for 5-star, with grumpy orange, neutral yellow and happy lime in between. Prefer plain stars? The robots are just the default skin of the same standard rating data.

Developed by Arun Thomas for ATV Software Labs.

Security

  • All admin actions are protected by nonces and the manage_woocommerce capability.
  • All input is sanitized server-side; all output is escaped.
  • Every database query uses $wpdb->prepare().
  • Direct file access is blocked in every PHP file.
sections.installation:
Installation

  1. Upload the atv-product-reviews-for-woocommerce folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the ZIP through Plugins → Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen.
  3. Make sure WooCommerce is installed and active (the plugin declares it as a dependency).
  4. Go to Products → Product Reviews and add your first review.

1. Add a review as the store owner

  1. Go to Products → Product Reviews.
  2. In the Add a new review card at the bottom, start typing a product name and pick one from the suggestions. You can attach the same review to several products at once — repeat the search to add more.
  3. Fill in the reviewer name (required), email (optional), a rating from 1 to 5, a title, the review text and the review date.
  4. Choose a status: Approved (counts toward the rating and the Google markup) or Pending (hidden from the storefront).
  5. Optionally tick Show “Verified purchase” badge.
  6. Click Save review. It appears in the reviews list on the same page.

2. Edit or moderate an existing review

  • Hover a review in the list and click Edit, or use the Approve / Set pending / Delete row actions.
  • The form pre-fills every field. Click Update review to save, or Cancel editing to go back.
  • Changing the linked products makes the review appear on, or disappear from, those products immediately.

3. Let customers review their purchases

  • No configuration needed. On any product page, the Reviews tab shows an Add Review button to logged-in customers who have purchased that product.
  • They pick a rating and (optionally) a title and review text, then click Submit Review. The review is published instantly and badged as a verified purchase.
  • A customer can review each product only once; the button is replaced by a thank-you note afterwards.
  • Guests and logged-in users who have not purchased the product see a note explaining that only verified buyers can review.

4. Ratings on your storefront

  • Approved reviews power the rating widget shown directly below the product title on single product pages and in shop/category loops.
  • Each rating is displayed as a row of five robot faces that all share the mood of the average score — from an angry red robot at 1 star to a joyful green robot at 5 stars.
  • The review count next to the rating is a link that opens the product’s Reviews tab.

5. Google rich results

  • Approved reviews are automatically added to your product pages as schema.org aggregateRating and review markup — no extra plugin or settings required.
  • To check a page, run its URL through Google’s Rich Results Test.
  • Pending reviews are excluded from the markup, so only reviews you have approved can influence your search results.

6. Track your reviews

  • The reviews list shows the rating, every linked product, the reviewer, the date, the status and the actions for each review.
  • Use the status filter and the search box to find reviews quickly; long lists are paginated.

7. Removing the plugin

  • Deactivating the plugin hides all ratings but keeps your reviews.
  • Deleting the plugin from the Plugins screen removes its custom tables and options permanently.
sections.faq:
When will star ratings appear in Google search results?

Rich results depend on Google’s crawling and indexing. Once your product pages are re-indexed, eligible products can show review stars. You can test your pages with Google’s Rich Results Test tool.

Does it work with my theme?

Yes. The rating widget hooks into WooCommerce’s standard template locations and a small script relocates it directly below the product title, so it stays correctly placed on virtually any theme.

Who can write reviews?

Two ways: you can add and manage reviews yourself from the dashboard, and any logged-in customer who has purchased the product can post their own review via the “Add Review” button in the Reviews tab. Submissions are verified against their orders automatically; guests see a friendly note instead.

Do pending reviews affect ratings?

No. Pending reviews stay hidden from the storefront and from the schema.org markup until you approve them.
